text:
incident-bot: Pager: elevated 5xx and tail latency for inference-proxy in az1a (region=us-east-1a). Spike started ~1725456750; 5xx rate ~8% over baseline, p99 latency >2s. Alert: inference-prod-route.

oncall-sre: Acked. I'm on it.

eng-runtime: seeing KV cache miss ratio jump for az1a services, also gRPC streams showing RESETs. Could be upstream network.

khan: Checking host metrics now — TX/RX errors low but retransmit count high on eni. Kernel: lots of SYN retransmits.

maya: From packet capture: many incomplete 3-way handshakes to NAT gw IPs, several connections falling back and re-opening.

infra-ops: AWS NATGateway metrics show active flows saturated and high connection churn in az1a. Possible SNAT port exhaustion pattern.

eng-runtime: That would cause many short-lived connections to fail -> 503s from proxy. Can we steer traffic away from az1a quickly?

oncall-sre: We have route weights set in control-plane. I'll shift traffic to az1b via a gradual weight change. Doing: `redwood route adjust --from az1a --to az1b --pct 50`

incident-bot: automsg: route-change requested by oncall-sre at 1725456842.

infra-ops: Confirmed TTLs for client-side DNS low (30s). But external customers may have sticky connections. We'll also temporarily increase proxy keepalive to reduce new connections.

eng-runtime: Applying keepalive tweak on proxy fleet in az1a: `env PROXY_KEEPALIVE=60 kubectl set env deploy/proxy -n inference PROXY_KEEPALIVE=60` — rolling update starting.

support-lead: Notifying top affected customers (ctrs 3/8 showing degraded 5xx). Drafting message.

oncall-sre: Traffic shift at 1725456900 -> az1b weight 80%. Monitoring.

maya: Early signal: 5xx rate for overall inference-prod dropped to 1.5% after shift, az1a still at 4% but decreasing. p99 latency back to ~300ms for az1b.

khan: Started draining new connections on a subset of az1a proxy instances to reduce churn. Marked instance group `proxy-az1a-spot-a` as `drain=true`.

infra-ops: Opened AWS support ticket (case #123456789) for NATGateway connection churn in az1a. Provided packet captures and CloudWatch metrics.

eng-runtime: Quick postmortem note: likely root cause = transient SNAT port exhaustion / connection laddering on AZ egress due to sudden spike in short-lived requests from batch job (identified later). Fallbacks behaved as designed (route weights + draining).

ops-mgr: Good work. Please record customer impact: 3 customers experienced increased 5xx/latency for ~12-18 minutes; no data exfiltration; system integrity intact.

support-lead: Sent customer-facing update to affected accounts at 1725457040.

oncall-sre: Handoff: I'm going to start an incident page and hand this to infra-ops for root-cause deep dive. infra-ops, please take ownership.

infra-ops: Taking over. Will collect logs, confirm whether NATGateway replacement or architecture change is needed (eg add ALB egress path or add nat pool).

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated: traffic steered and proxies drained, overall 5xx returned to baseline at 1725457060. RCA in progress.

ops-mgr: Planning follow-up: schedule a post-incident review + mitigation plan (increase NAT headroom, long-lived conn recommendations, control-plane auto-steer runbook).

khan: Saving key snippets for RCA: `netstat -tn | grep ESTAB | wc -l` peaked at ~120k on proxy hosts; connection churn metrics attached to the ticket.

eng-runtime: Also adding a runtime safeguard: if KV miss ratio > 5% and 5xx > 2% in an AZ, auto-reduce weight for that AZ by 70% (canary rule). Will open PR for the ramp policy.

ops-mgr: Handshake complete. Handoff note: infra-ops now P0 incident owner. oncall-sre stepping back to follow-up.

infra-ops: Acknowledged. Will update when we hear back from AWS support.

support-lead: Final customer note queued; follow-up with customers after RCA. :white_check_mark:
